newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee roaster keeps price options open.
newsitem.headline: German coffee roaster keeps price options open.

text.p: German coffee market leader Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS) said it would keep open its option of raising ex-plant prices of roasted coffee for a third time this year although coffee futures were headed sharply lower.
"The warning signs have not been switched off...sharp futures losses represent profit-taking rather than changes in fundamentals," said spokesman Rolf Sauerbier in response to an inquiry.
He said Brazil's crop was at its most vulnerable stage and possible weather damage had not been ruled out.
Markets plummeted in June after 20-year highs in May on supply tightness because of signs supplies could become more comfortable.
Colombia has reopened export registrations and Brazil may be set for a better crop, according to latest U.S. government forecasts.
But Sauerbier said prices were at historically high levels -- New York July arabicas last traded at around 193 cents.
Actual retail levels in Germany's competitive market were still not reflecting higher raw materials and currency costs.
KJS, part of Philip Morris Cos Inc, had not shelved plans to raise price again after combined price rises by 2.50 per 500 grams earlier this year, Sauerbier said.
But it could not specify the possible increase, nor indicate its timing.
Competitor Tchibo last week said it would raise its prices per 500 grams by 0.70 marks as of June 26 from the current range of 8.99-10.99 marks.
